plain_english_title: Gulf War Undiagnosed/Multisymptom Illnesses, PACT Act Burn Pit Presumptions & Toxic Exposure (TERA) Exams
what_this_means: Veterans who served in Southwest Asia or expanded post-9/11 theaters—and Veterans from any era exposed to occupational or environmental hazards—have three distinct paths to service connection that VA examiners sometimes confuse: (1) Gulf War presumptions under 38 U.S.C. § 1117 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.317 for undiagnosed illnesses and Medically Unexplained Chronic Multisymptom Illnesses (chronic fatigue syndrome, fibromyalgia, and functional gastrointestinal disorders like irritable bowel syndrome), which require NO medical nexus opinion; (2) PACT Act airborne-hazard and burn-pit presumptions (38 U.S.C. § 1120 and 38 C.F.R. §§ 3.320–3.320b) covering more than two dozen respiratory conditions and cancers; and (3) direct Toxic Exposure Risk Activity (TERA) medical nexus exams under 38 U.S.C. § 1168 for non-presumptive conditions linked to jet fuel, PFAS firefighting foam, solvents, radiation, or burn pits.
record_clues: A DD-214, deployment travel voucher, flight log, or Individual Longitudinal Exposure Record (ILER) showing service on or after August 2, 1990 in Southwest Asia/Somalia, or on or after September 11, 2001 in Afghanistan, Djibouti, Syria, Jordan, Egypt, Lebanon, Yemen, or Uzbekistan (K2).

A VA exam denying fibromyalgia, chronic fatigue syndrome, irritable bowel syndrome, or chronic unexplained joint/muscle pain because 'there is no medical nexus linking the condition to Gulf War service.'
A pre-August 10, 2022 denial of asthma, rhinitis, or sinusitis because symptoms started more than 10 years after discharge or were rated below 10%.

A diagnosis of urinary bladder or ureter cancer (§ 3.320a, effective January 2, 2025) or leukemia, multiple myeloma, MGUS, myelodysplastic syndrome, or myelofibrosis (§ 3.320b, effective January 10, 2025), or a negative TERA medical opinion that ignored military occupational specialty chemical exposures.
important_cautions: Different effective-date rules apply to living Veterans vs. Survivors: unlike Vietnam Nehmer claims, PACT Act burn-pit presumptions for living Veterans generally cannot take effect earlier than August 10, 2022 (or January 2025 for newly added §§ 3.320a–3.320b cancers) under 38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a), whereas previously denied Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) survivor claims re-evaluated under 38 U.S.C. § 1305 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.33 can reach back to the original DIC claim date.

Statutory text overrides lagging print regulations: the PACT Act (August 10, 2022) statutorily removed the Dec. 31, 2026 Gulf War deadline and added Afghanistan, Israel, Egypt, Turkey, Syria, and Jordan to 38 U.S.C. § 1117, even while VA's October 1, 2024 conforming regulation (89 FR 79815) remains a proposed rule that is not finalized. Similarly, RIN 2900-AQ72 (sleep apnea) remains an unfinalized proposed rule.

Conditions with a known or partially explained pathology (such as diabetes, multiple sclerosis, or obstructive sleep apnea) do not qualify as unexplained illnesses under 38 C.F.R. § 3.317(a), so representatives typically pursue them through a § 1168 TERA nexus opinion or § 3.310 secondary connection.

Failures to order a TERA exam or search ILER records are duty-to-assist errors addressed through open review lanes (Higher-Level Review, Supplemental Claim, or Board appeal), not Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) motions (Cook v. Principi; 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c)).
questions_for_representative: Does my diagnosed condition already qualify as a presumptive Gulf War multisymptom illness (§ 3.317) or PACT Act burn-pit respiratory/cancer condition (§§ 3.320–3.320b) where no medical nexus opinion is needed?
Have we requested my Individual Longitudinal Exposure Record (ILER) and military occupational exposure history before attending a 38 U.S.C. § 1168 TERA medical exam?

If VA denied my PACT Act or Gulf War condition before August 10, 2022 (or before January 2025 for newly added blood and bladder cancers), should we file a Supplemental Claim and check the liberalizing effective-date rules?
If I am a surviving spouse whose DIC claim was previously denied, am I eligible for retroactive re-evaluation back to my original DIC filing date under 38 U.S.C. § 1305 and 38 C.F.R. § 3.33?
